population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈270M, so 32.5% ≈ 87.8M current users. Persistence: of the 27.9 pts on in 2032, 57% (15.9) stayed on through 2034. That is down from 60% because employer weight-only coverage fell and conditioned users were dropped. The 12.0 who stopped joined the 9.1 already off, a pool of 21.1. Of that pool 50% (10.6) restarted, down from 57%, because restarting now often means paying cash, which leaves 10.5 off. New ever-users numbered 7.4 pts: 6.0 on and 1.4 already off. Check: on = 15.9 + 10.6 + 6.0 = 32.5. Off = 10.5 + 1.4 = 11.9. Ever = 37.0 + 7.4 = 44.4 = 32.5 + 11.9. Cycled: the 13.4 pts who had cycled by 2032, plus ~6.5 pts of first-time restarters, plus ~0.4 among new starters, give 20.3 of 44.4 = 46%. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23%: 3.8 + 11.88 + 12.0 + 4.83 = 32.5. The 65+ figure of 21% (≈13.0M) is driven by the dementia label and Part D diabetes and cardiovascular coverage, and is held back by DEXA gates. Income thirds: (41 + 30 + 26.5)/3 = 32.5. The middle third grew least (28→30) because it is where employer weight-only coverage was withdrawn. The bottom (21.7→26.5) grew through Medicaid's diabetes and cardiac codes, HRSA liraglutide and $149 oral starts. The top (34→41) grew through cash retatrutide and the bimagrumab add-on. Off-drug: ≈32.1M adults (11.9%) have used and are off now, and roughly 6–7M of them were displaced by employer withdrawal rather than by choice or side effects. Never-users: ≈150M (55.6%), including organised refusers, uninsured adults in non-expansion states and people with contraindications. Pediatric: 1.4% of ~73M ≈ 1.02M, of whom ~190k are aged 6–11. Two cohorts of children have now grown up eating at tables where the adults are on drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: carried forward unchanged through Dec 2035 in the December 2033 year-end extenders package, with no new terms. Payment follows the existing Strategic Supply Agreement formula to $199/month from Jan 2034. The copay stays $50. Conditions are unchanged: ≥5% loss at month 6, ≥80% PDC, and DEXA plus a resistance-training referral for 65+. Bridge obesity users ≈4.0M: 4.0M × $199 × 12 ≈ $9.55B/yr. Medicare overall pays 15.5% of adult fills ≈ 13.6M users (≈13.0M aged 65+ plus ~0.6M disabled under-65). The other ~9.6M are covered under Part D for diabetes, cardiovascular, CKD, OSA, MASH and now dementia-risk codes. Medicaid pays 12.0% ≈ 10.5M users at $199: 10.5M × $199 × 12 ≈ $25.1B/yr combined federal and state. There are still seven adherence waivers and no new ones. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program: flat at $5.0B under full-year continuing resolutions for FY2033 and FY2034, and still unconditional. It serves ≈3.9M: 2.6M generic liraglutide × $60 × 12 ≈ $1.87B, plus 1.3M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $159 × 12 ≈ $2.48B, total ≈ $4.35B. TRICARE, the VA and the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program cover ≈2.6M, including ~150k active duty in the readiness programme: 150k × $149 × 12 ≈ $268M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $6–35/month, and generic tirzepatide is sold in India, Brazil, Turkey, Egypt and Indonesia. Generic semaglutide is standard across Canada, Mexico, China and most of Latin America and Asia. Chinese originator triple agonists are on the market domestically and are exported to ASEAN and Gulf states. US entry of generic semaglutide slipped past 2034 after the FDA's November 2033 complete response letters to the first synthetic-peptide ANDAs over impurity and immunogenicity comparability. The settlements' entry dates were contingent on approval.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~87.8M adult users: commercial 31.0% (27.2M), Medicare 15.5% (13.6M), Medicaid 12.0% (10.5M), HRSA 4.4% (3.9M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.0% (2.6M), cash/direct 23.2% (20.4M), gray 10.9% (9.6M); total 100%. Managed decline continued. The January 2034 Strategic Supply Agreement step moved TrumpRx/direct prices to $199 (semaglutide injection), $249 (tirzepatide) and $299 (retatrutide). The $149 oral start price is unchanged. Amycretin launched at $299 direct. The bimagrumab add-on is $849/month direct ($1,450 list) and is almost never covered, so the combination with tirzepatide costs ~$1,098 a month in cash. Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. Employer retreat: weight-management coverage fell from 63% to 50% of employers after the May 2033 Sixth Circuit ruling removed PBM adherence feeds as a basis for premium differentials. Plans now cover incretins on diagnosis codes: T2D, established CVD, OSA, MASH, CKD, and two psychiatric codes, BED and, from Aug 2034, gambling disorder. The psychiatric codes are protected by mental-health parity, which has made diagnosis-code shopping a recognised pattern. Commercial users fell from 28.8M to 27.2M even as total use rose. About 6–7M people lost weight-only coverage, about half moved to cash, and the rest stopped or went gray. Gray users rose slightly in absolute terms (9.0→9.6M) but fell as a share, because $199 branded semaglutide undercuts many 503A compounders. Skip-but-fill declined among commercial users whose plans dropped adherence gating. It persists in the Bridge and the seven Medicaid waivers. Cash cyclers now buy in 'two on, one off' patterns.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance; T2D indication Mar 2033)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin dual agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Oct 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist driver is realised through an existing product, as the approval rules require. Retatrutide (already at 30.4% mean loss on the 12 mg dose) gained a T2D glycaemic indication in Mar 2033. That opened coverage under diabetes codes just as employers dropped weight-only coverage. Its direct price fell to $299 in Jan 2034, making it the leading new start among cash payers. No new US triple agonist is approved: Novo's licensed UBT251 is in phase 3 with no filing, and Chinese originator triple agonists are sold only outside the US. Amycretin, under review at the start of the window, was approved Oct 2033 (~22% loss at 68 weeks) and is supply-limited. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide, filed Mar 2032, received a CRL in Mar 2033 on manufacturing and was approved Feb 2034. It preserves ~60–70% of the lean mass otherwise lost, with no fracture-outcome data. The gambling-disorder label rests on a 26-week randomised trial: ~2.1 fewer gambling days per week than placebo and a 38% vs 22% responder rate. The effect waned on discontinuation. The market is ≈$180B globally in 2034: US users +17% over two years and US net price −10 to −12%. Generic semaglutide in the US is delayed past 2034 by complete response letters; generic_us remains false.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are highest on retatrutide 12 mg and among cash cyclers who restart without re-titrating. Lawyer advertising now shapes symptom reporting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; FDA re-titration guidance after gaps of more than two weeks (2033).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mass-tort scale. MDL 3094 had ~148,000 filed and tolled claims by mid-2034, up from ~61,000, recruited by television and social ads aimed at long-term users and cyclers. In Mar 2034 Novo announced a $3.6B settlement programme for gastroparesis, ileus and obstruction claims against its products, conditional on 90% participation and without admission. Lilly declined to join and is trying cases. Of seven bellwethers so far, four went to plaintiffs. Persistence after stopping remains scientifically disputed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In Jun 2034 FDA added reports of gastroparesis persisting after discontinuation to the Postmarketing Experience section, but still declines a Warnings-level causal statement. Reserves are up again in the 2033 annual reports.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases are rising with retatrutide volume and faster loss.

A Sentinel analysis (2033) finds a modest dose-related excess with retatrutide 12 mg (~0.4 vs ~0.25 per 100 patient-years) that is confounded by gallstones and rapid loss. Registries for other agents show low absolute risk. The pancreatitis track in the MDL and the Philadelphia mass-tort programme has ~31,000 claims. A Philadelphia jury awarded $38M against Lilly in Apr 2034, and the verdict is on appeal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; FDA requested a dedicated retatrutide pancreatic-safety observational study (PMR, 2033).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. Plaintiffs filed a cancer track in 2033. Large Nordic and US registries show no increase, and FDA and EMA find no causal signal. Claims number in the low thousands, but the ads that recruit them reach millions.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. The MDL judge is holding a Rule 702 expert hearing on general causation, with no ruling yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Remains a population problem, and is now visibly class-graded. Users with trainers, protein and bimagrumab preserve mass. Users on liraglutide and compounded product mostly do not. NHANES-DXA has not been updated since the 2029–31 cycle.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings retained. The Bridge requires a training referral. Bimagrumab is approved but covered by almost no plan or public programme, and a HELP Committee letter (2034) asks CMS why Medicare does not cover it.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions are up again, ~3% over 2032–33. Modelled excess ≈ 13.0M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr baseline × HR ~0.30 (somewhat reduced by antiresorptive cover) ≈ 19,500 hip fractures a year, concentrated in women and cyclers. The final adolescent bone-accrual study (2033) confirmed lumbar-spine z-score accrual ~0.15–0.2 SD lower after more than 3 years on drug. Weight-loss confounding is acknowledged but not thought to explain all of it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Baseline DEXA for 65+ and postmenopausal women stays in Warnings. The FDA pediatric labelling update (Oct 2033) adds bone-age and DEXA monitoring for adolescents on drug more than 2 years. Bridge DEXA is unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the BED, AUD and gambling-disorder trial populations.

Long-term users still report reduced pleasure at ~10–15%. In the gambling-disorder trial, SHAPS anhedonia shifts were ~6% vs 3%, which the sponsor describes as on-mechanism. Deliberate dose holidays: ~48% of long-term users in the past year, with cash payers the most likely to holiday.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label section and class precaution unchanged; the gambling label carries the same precaution. The Foundayo BED label was revised in 2034 to require a structured diagnostic interview, as part of the DOJ resolution.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now driven mainly by employer withdrawal of weight-only coverage (~6–7M displaced), as well as Bridge and Medicaid cut-offs. Partial restarts on cash produce sawtooth weight curves.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D insufficiency signals persist and are worst among HRSA, gray and cash-cycling users without dietetic support.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Bridge counselling includes a protein target.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult follow-up. ~190k children aged 6–11 are on drug. The first pubertal-timing data (2034 registry interim) are inconclusive: there is a small shift toward later menarche in girls on drug before age 11, and the cohort is small.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry continues; FDA pediatric label update Oct 2033 (bone monitoring).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls are flat. Compounded-semaglutide dosing errors persist among users displaced from employer coverage. Research-peptide retatrutide is marginal at a $299 branded price, while research-peptide bimagrumab analogues have appeared in gyms.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CBP mail seizures continue; a second federal distributor indictment (2033); FDA import alert on unapproved activin-receptor antibodies (2034).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; rising in absolute numbers with volume.

'Brain health' use among 50–64-year-olds outside the label continues to grow and is now often paid in cash after employer weight coverage ended. These users carry the bone and muscle risk with no proven cognitive benefit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label states the population limits; no enforcement against off-label prescribing.

safety_ledger.effect: Off-label psychiatric promotion and screen inflation (BED, compulsion)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. Low-dose Foundayo BED users peaked at ~3.4M in mid-2033 against an estimated ~1.5–2M treatable BED population, then fell to ~2.2M after the settlement. Telehealth 'compulsion' assessments are rising after the gambling label.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DOJ/HHS-OIG settlement with Lilly ($2.4B, May 2034) with a five-year corporate integrity agreement; revised BED labelling requires a structured diagnosis.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. In gambling-trial follow-up, gambling days returned to baseline within ~8–12 weeks of stopping, much as weight returns. Clinicians report users timing dose holidays around sports seasons.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The label states the effect is not durable after discontinuation; long-term extension study required.

food_and_beverage.state: US packaged-food volume keeps falling at ~2% a year, slightly slower as the base shrinks. The market has split by class. Premium protein, 'muscle-tier' leucine and creatine formats sell at Whole Foods and gym counters. Dollar stores and private equity–owned indulgent brands sell larger value packs to the off-drug and displaced middle. Ohio and Michigan grocers report the clearest split, store by store, along income lines.

alcohol.state: US spirits and beer volume fell for a sixth year. AUD coverage, HRSA cessation and 32% of adults on drug keep consumption down. Tasting-room and premium single-serve formats hold value while light-beer volume erodes. State excise forecasts keep the incretin line.

restaurants.state: Mid-income suburban value chains keep closing units. Fine dining in affluent metros adapts with tasting-menu 'small courses' priced high. Buffets and value chains in lower-income areas hold up slightly better than expected because off-drug and displaced customers stay loyal. Sports bars near casinos report softer late-night tabs.

apparel.state: Fit is class-coded. Tailors and premium athletic brands cut for muscled lean bodies. Mass retailers stock wide and shifting size runs for cyclers whose weight goes up and down. Uniform makers continue military and police re-cuts.

fitness.state: Strength studios charging $200–400 a month bundle trainers, DEXA and bimagrumab concierge referrals for the top third. Low-cost gyms fill with Bridge and Medicare Advantage referrals. Gyms that sold access to employer-plan members lose some volume as conditions lapse.

insurance.state: Employer weight-only coverage fell to 50% of employers after the Sixth Circuit ruling removed adherence-based premium differentials, and stop-loss carriers 'laser' weight-only incretin claims. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac, renal, hepatic and psychiatric codes. PBMs now sell diagnosis-code audit services in place of adherence verification. Pharmacy trend is ~+7%.

pharma.state: Lilly remains national champion and price setter, with a $2.4B settlement and a corporate integrity agreement. Its DPA plants and DoD and VA supply make the Strategic Supply Agreement politically sturdy. Novo's margins are squeezed by tariff, matched pricing and a $3.6B MDL programme, partly offset by amycretin and the gambling label. Generic semaglutide makers wait on FDA. Indian API exposure remains a board risk for compounders.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now reads as income more than compliance. A dense, muscled lean body with good posture signals cash: retatrutide, bimagrumab, a trainer, protein and a DEXA history. A thin, soft 'pen-thin' body signals the middle: $199 semaglutide or the $149 pill, no coaching. A body whose weight rises and falls signals the cycler who lost employer coverage. A heavier body is read as either priced out or refusing, and strangers can't tell which.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: 'Muscle tier' is now the stated term in Charlotte, Scottsdale and north Dallas: bimagrumab add-on at $849 a month on top of the incretin, plus trainers. In Dayton and Toledo, where the Sixth Circuit ruling hit employer plans first, office workers who lost coverage are visibly regaining weight within a year. Among older women in Sun City, posture and a fall-free year still mark the affluent.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Eating has split by class. Affluent households hold small-plate 'protein suppers' as status meals. Value buffets and church potlucks serve the off-drug and the displaced. Open Table suppers continue in Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa, and now attract laid-off-coverage cyclers as well as refusers. School nutritionists report children of muscle-tier parents bringing protein packs to lunch.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule and now the tier ('reta + bima'). Muscle-tier bodies are openly read as a sign of money. Couples where one partner lost employer coverage argue over whether a household budget covers two cash prescriptions or one.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is clinical, coded and priced. Weight-only hunger is no longer covered, while 'compulsive' hunger under a BED or gambling code is. The backlash still preaches 'hunger is how we were made', and the Lilly settlement gave it a documented example of pharmaceutical overreach.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure, and ~48% took at least one deliberate holiday last year. Cash payers holiday most because nobody tracks them. Skip-but-fill persists only in the Bridge and the Medicaid waivers. Low-dose Foundayo BED users are ~2.2M (peak ~3.4M) and gambling-label semaglutide has ~0.3M by year-end. Both sit inside the commercial, Medicaid and cash shares. Quiet-subscription telehealth is down to ~0.8M as 'compulsion' assessments replace it.
interior_life.framing: 'The grey' is still a complaint. It is also, under codes, a treatment for gambling and bingeing. After the Lilly settlement it carries a third name: a product that was marketed past its label. Clinicians say 'reward modulation'; sportsbook ads joke that 'the house always wins—unless you're on the pen'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: With fewer employers gating on adherence, dose holidays are self-scheduled: sales staff skip at quarter-end, nurses before vacations. Muscle-tier executives cultivate a 'calm' that subordinates read as money. Police and military programmes still track tape and DEXA, not mood.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Off-dose billing is routine. Sports-betting operators in New Jersey and Ohio cite incretin use for handle softness in earnings calls, and responsible-gaming funds in two states pay for counselling referrals that now come with a prescription. Comedy about the grey has moved on to jokes about being 'pen-thin'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Holidays around anniversaries and conception attempts remain routine. Sex therapists see couples where the drug was prescribed for compulsive sexual behaviour off-label, and where the partner calls the result peace and the patient calls it absence.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Lilly settlement handed the anti-pharma, religious and fat-liberation coalition its first documented scandal, and 2034 midterm candidates are asked about it. Pro-access populists defend TrumpRx prices and blame employers for retreating. Neither bloc has proposed new law this cycle. Displaced middle-income cyclers are courted by both and belong to neither.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access, price-managing and largely static. FDA approved amycretin, bimagrumab and the gambling label and acted on pediatric bone through labelling. No new federal or state policy was adopted in the window. Enforcement action came through DOJ settlement and customs, not new rules.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Existing channels persist without new terms. The Medicare Bridge was carried forward unchanged in the year-end extenders, at $199 under the existing SSA formula with a $50 copay. HRSA was flat at $5.0B under continuing resolutions. The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program continues, as does the ACA cessation mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning has receded in the commercial market after the Sixth Circuit ruling. A Fifth Circuit decision upheld the 2031 guidance, leaving a circuit split and a pending cert petition. Conditioning remains entrenched in the public channels: the Bridge, the seven Medicaid adherence waivers and the military tape and DEXA tracking. PBMs have shifted from adherence surveillance to diagnosis-code audits. The Tennessee and Idaho premium-conditioning bans stand.
state.workforce_or_military: The readiness programme is at ~150k active duty with Guard pilots ongoing. Body-composition separations remain ~30% below the 2030 baseline. Religious-accommodation requests number ~3,100 cumulative. Big-city police and fire contracts continue. No new workforce programmes.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 critical-medicine duties and Lilly's national-champion status are unchanged. Novo pays duty on Danish API. India's WTO dispute has moved to panel stage with no ruling. Chinese originator triple agonists are exported across ASEAN and the Gulf, creating the first non-US-originated next-gen products abroad. Global South markets run on Indian generics.

events.event: Sixth Circuit vacates the part of the 2031 tri-agency wellness guidance that let employers use PBM adherence feeds for premium differentials, citing evidence that skip-but-fill makes the data unreliable. The Fifth Circuit upheld it in February. Within two benefit cycles, employer weight-management coverage falls from 63% to 50%, and plans shift coverage to diagnosis codes.

Strategic Supply Agreement price step takes effect: TrumpRx semaglutide $199, tirzepatide $249, retatrutide (newly labelled for type 2 diabetes since March 2033) $299. It follows FDA complete response letters in November 2033 to the first generic semaglutide applications, which push US generic entry past 2034.

FDA approves bimagrumab as a lean-mass-preserving add-on to tirzepatide. Lilly lists it at $849 a month direct. No major PBM formulary or Medicare plan covers it at launch, while concierge strength studios in Charlotte and Scottsdale sell 'muscle tier' packages around it.

Novo Nordisk announces a $3.6 billion programme to settle gastroparesis, ileus and obstruction claims in MDL 3094, which has grown to about 148,000 claims. Lilly refuses to join, and a Philadelphia jury awards $38 million in a retatrutide pancreatitis case the next month.

Eli Lilly pays $2.4 billion and signs a five-year corporate integrity agreement to resolve a whistleblower suit, unsealed in September 2033, alleging it designed telehealth 'binge-eating screens' to steer non-BED patients onto low-dose Foundayo under the 'quiet the noise around food' campaign. FDA requires a structured diagnosis in revised labelling. The Strategic Supply Agreement is untouched.

FDA approves semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly as an adjunct to counselling for gambling disorder in adults, the first incretin label for a behavioural addiction outside substances and food. Mental-health parity rules oblige most commercial plans to cover it.

open_tensions: Coverage now follows diagnosis codes, and the psychiatric ones (BED, gambling) are protected by parity while weight-only obesity is not. Telehealth 'compulsion' assessments are growing in a market where the leading manufacturer has just admitted screen inflation. PBM code audits and parity enforcement are on a collision course.

The circuit split on adherence-based wellness differentials is before the Supreme Court on cert. Meanwhile the public channels (Bridge, seven Medicaid waivers, military tape and DEXA) still ration with the adherence data the Sixth Circuit called unreliable.

Lilly is simultaneously the federal price setter, the DoD and VA supplier, a company under a corporate integrity agreement, and the main holdout in a ~148,000-claim mass tort. Delayed US generic semaglutide removes the one external check on the bargain, and India's WTO panel and Novo's tariff burden remain live.

Muscle preservation is now a purchasable product (bimagrumab at $849 cash) that Medicare does not cover, while ~13M users aged 65+ carry a modelled ~19,500 excess hip fractures a year. Pressure for Medicare coverage of an expensive add-on with no fracture-outcome data is building against flat budgets.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: The Muscle Tier: In 2034 You Can Read an American's Paycheck From Across the Room
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2034 almost one American adult in three is on an incretin drug, about eighty-eight million people. More than forty-four percent have used one at some point, and nearly half of those have stopped and started again at least once. Over two years the drug got cheaper. Covering it under an ordinary employer plan got harder.

The break came from a courtroom. In May 2033 the Sixth Circuit struck down the rule that had let employers set premiums from pharmacy adherence data. The court accepted what everyone in the business knew: people picked up refills they never injected, so the data were fiction. Without that tool, employers that had covered weight loss on conditions looked at the bill and many stopped covering it. Half of employers still cover it. The rest cover the drug only for a diagnosis: diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea, a failing liver or kidney. Some six or seven million people lost weight-only coverage. About half now pay cash and the rest stopped or went to compounders. In Dayton and Toledo you can watch it happen on bodies within a year.

Cash is cheaper than it was. In January the federal price deal with Eli Lilly stepped down again: semaglutide at $199 a month, tirzepatide at $249, and retatrutide, the triple agonist that takes off about thirty percent of body weight, at $299. Retatrutide picked up a diabetes label the previous spring, so it now gets covered under the diabetes codes. Generic semaglutide was supposed to arrive in 2033. In November the FDA sent the first applications back over impurity questions, and the date slipped. Novo matched Lilly's prices and keeps paying tariff.

Above the cash tier sits a higher one. In February the FDA approved bimagrumab, an antibody that preserves most of the muscle weight loss would otherwise take. It costs $849 a month, and almost no plan covers it. Strength studios in Charlotte and Scottsdale now build memberships around it. The look that results is dense, upright and lean, and people call it the muscle tier. Below it is 'pen-thin': the soft thinness of a $199 pen without a trainer. Below that is the cycler's sawtooth. Heavier people, as ever, are read either as priced out or as refusers.

The drugs also moved further into behaviour. In August semaglutide was approved for gambling disorder. Mental-health parity law makes most plans cover it, so in the new code-based system a psychiatric diagnosis can be a route to the drug. That arrived three months after Lilly paid $2.4 billion to settle a whistleblower case. The suit showed that its telehealth partners had tuned binge-eating screens to put people without the disorder on low-dose Foundayo, which the ads had promised would 'quiet the noise around food.' The settlement brought a five-year integrity agreement, but the federal supply deal survived. The Pentagon and the VA depend on Lilly's plants.

The lawsuits got bigger as well. The federal gastroparesis litigation now holds about 148,000 claims, recruited by late-night ads. In March Novo offered $3.6 billion to settle without admitting fault. Lilly is fighting, and a Philadelphia jury gave a pancreatitis plaintiff $38 million.

Government mostly stood still. The Medicare Bridge rolled forward unchanged in the year-end extenders, at $199 with a $50 copay and the same bone-scan and weight-loss conditions. The free community-clinic programme was flat-funded. The seven Medicaid adherence waivers are still in force. Hip fractures among older users keep rising slowly.

Nearly half of long-term users still take breaks from the drug to get back what they call the grey. Fewer of them now fake their refills, because fewer insurers are watching. Sportsbooks blame the pen for softer handle. Two years after the last crisis, things look calm.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Kowalczyk, forty-four, opens the dental office in Kettering at seven-ten and turns on the sterilizer. The plan letter is still pinned to the corkboard in the break room: effective January 1, weight management benefits are discontinued; diabetes and cardiovascular coverage unaffected. Her A1c is 5.9. She checked twice.

She has three semaglutide pens from TrumpRx in the fridge at home, $199 each, bought in January. This month is the off month. By ten she is hungry in a way she had forgotten, and she eats two of the hygienist's clementines standing up.

Dr. Halvorsen comes in at nine with a protein shaker and forearms like rope. He is fifty-eight and stands perfectly straight. His bimagrumab infusion is on the shared calendar as 'personal.'

At lunch Marisol says her telehealth doctor asked forty minutes of questions this time, not six, before renewing her Foundayo. 'Since the settlement,' she says. 'They want you to really have it.'

A patient's mother asks if braces fit differently on kids whose parents are on the pen. Dana says she doesn't know.

After work she drives past the Golden Corral, which is full, and the new strength studio on Far Hills, which is lit and nearly empty. Membership is $340 a month.

At home her husband Rick, off since the Ohio waiver locked him out two years ago, is frying onions. A lawyer on television asks whether she has ever felt full for too long.

She eats a full plate. It tastes like something. She marks the calendar: restart Sunday.
